'''Frank Robinson Hartley''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]] [[FRAeS]] (born 29 January 1942)<ref name ="WW">
{{Citation
| url   = http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U19334
| title = HARTLEY, Prof. Frank Robinson'
| work =  Who's Who 2013, A & C Black
| publisher = Bloomsbury Publishing plc, 2013; online edn, Oxford University Press, Dec 2013; online edn, Dec 2015
| accessdate = 27 Dec 2015
}}</ref> is a former [[vice-chancellor]] of [[Cranfield University]] (previously the  Cranfield Institute of Technology) from 1989 to 2006.<ref name = "WW"/>

==Early life and career==
He was the son of [[Frank Hartley (pharmacist)|Sir Frank Hartley CBE]]<ref>{{Cite news |last=Florence |first=A.T. |date=19 February 1997 |title=Obituary: Sir Frank Hartley |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituary-sir-frank-hartley-1279450.html |access-date=30 July 2024 |work=The Independent}}</ref> a former vice chancellor of [[London University]].<ref name = "WW"/> He was educated at [[King's College School, Wimbledon]], London, and [[Magdalen College]], [[Oxford University|Oxford]].<ref name = "WW"/>

==Career==
He was post-doctoral fellow in protein chemistry at the [[Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation]] in  [[Melbourne]] from 1966 to 1969. He was then [[Imperial Chemical Industries]] Research Fellow and tutor in [[physical chemistry]] at [[University College London]] from 1969 to 1970. From 1970 to 1975 he was lecturer in [[inorganic chemistry]] at the [[University of Southampton]].<ref name = "WW"/>

He then joined the [[Royal Military College of Science]], [[Shrivenham]] (RMCS), as professor of chemistry and head of the department of chemistry and metallurgy from 1975 to 1982, acting dean from 1982 to 1984, principal and dean from 1984 to 1989. From 1989 to 1990 he was director of Cranfield Institute of Technology (CIT – later [[Cranfield University]]) which was incorporated by Royal Charter in 1969 – an academic partnership (RMCS) had been formed in 1984. He was vice-chancellor of [[Cranfield University]] from 1989 to 2006.<ref name = "WW"/>

==Personal life==
He married first, 1964, Valerie Peel (died 2005), and they had three daughters. He married second, 2009, Charmaine Harvey.

==Publications==
{{Div col|colwidth=30em}}
* "The Chemistry of Platinum and Palladium", Applied Science, 1973<ref name = "WW"/>
* "Elements of Organometallic Chemistry", Chemical Society, 1974, {{ISBN|0851869092}} with C Burgess and R M Alcock <ref name = "WW"/>
* "Solution Equilibria", 1985
* "The Chemistry of the Metal-Carbon Bond", Vol 1 1983, Vol 2 1984, Vol 3 1985, Vol 4 1987, Vol 5 1989 (with S Patel)
* "The Chemistry of Organophosphorus Coumpounds" Vol 2-4 1990-1996
* "Supported Metal Complexes" 1989
* "The chemistry of the Platinum Group Metals", 1991
{{div col end}}
